# Implementation

## Changed behavior

The intake parser now explicitly selects version 1 when `formatVersion` is omitted or `1`, and version 2 only when the numeric value is `2`. Other selector values are invalid. Version 1 validation and canonical output remain unchanged.

Version 2 rows and single submissions accept `amount.decimal`, optionally `amount.currency`, and optionally `shipOn` as `{ year, month, day }`. Decimal amounts are parsed exactly into integer cents within `1..1,000,000`; currency defaults only when omitted and must be exactly `USD` when present. Date components are validated as real Gregorian dates in years `2000..2099` and formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD`. When the whole version 2 `shipOn` property is omitted, the parser uses the call's trusted `context.receivedOn`.

All accepted orders are still saved and returned with exactly `id`, `customerId`, `amountCents`, `currency`, `shipOn`, and `receivedOn`.

## Affected call paths

`submitOrder` and each `importOrders` row now call `parseOrder(value, context)` so version 2 date defaulting uses the same host context as saving. The existing `saveOrder` path remains responsible for duplicate detection, storage failures, canonical order construction, and response status mapping. Batch summaries continue to use only rows whose `saveOrder` call completed with status `201`.

## Justified deviations

The implementation keeps the existing simple `undefined` parse-failure convention instead of introducing a Result library because the project has no Result dependency and the public response mapping already centralizes validation failure as `{ code: "invalid_order" }`.

## Remaining limitations

The service still relies on the documented repository guarantees for failed saves and duplicate visibility. It does not add migration, damaged-record repair, retries, clock reads, concurrency control, or all-or-nothing batch behavior.
